text:
Alex Morgan: Heads up — seeing repeated tail-latency spikes (~p99 1.2s from baseline ~250ms) on eu-west dedicated pool during large inference batches from tenant-gamma. Pattern looks like bursts every 15-20m lasting ~3-5m. Any obvious suspects?
Priya Shah: rough q — is this purely GPU compute or is egress/egress-queueing showing up? can you paste the net/egress counters? :thinking_face: 
Alex Morgan: quick dump attached inline: ```egress_tx_queue: backlog=128k pkts; nic_tx_drops=0; gpu_util: 72%; nvlink_tx: 9.8GB/s; p99_latency_ms: 1200; active_tenants_on_node: [tenant-gamma, tenant-beta, infra-test]``` Not seeing kernel drops but queue backlog spikes.
Mateo Ruiz: hmm NVLink numbers look high — could be cross-tenant memory traffic (kv-cache churn) + large batch KV reads. We've seen similar when a tenant does big multi-query beam searches. Any chance tenant-gamma switched to multi-beam?
Alex Morgan: they pushed a change yesterday to increase beam_width=8 for rerank. Timing lines up.
Claire Thompson: we could try soft-segregation: route tenant-gamma to a burst-bridge (preemptible/high-egress) slice while they run heavy jobs. Tradeoff: cost + slightly higher tail for them but protective for others.
Jin Park: FYI I've got a small scheduler patch that biases allocations with high RDMA/NVLink usage to fractional-dedicated slices. Flag is `--soft-isolate-high-egress=true`. Rolling it to canary might help without full dedicated carveout. Command to flip in console: `curl -X POST $ORCH/api/v1/policies/flags -d '{"soft_isolate_high_egress":true, "scope":"eu-west"}'` (use admin token).
Alex Morgan: can you roll to eu-west canary now? I can coordinate with tenant-gamma to throttle beam width if needed.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy update submitted by jin; rollout started to canary eu-west at 2026-03-22T09:17:50Z.
Priya Shah: quick telemetry check after ~4m of canary: p99 dropped from 1200ms -> ~320ms on affected nodes, nvlink_tx per-node down ~30%. Looks promising.
Mateo Ruiz: if canary holds, next step is to add a metric alert to detect beam-width-ish jumps and autoschedule soft-isolate.
Claire Thompson: also log cost delta for the burst bridge fallback so we can evaluate net cost vs SLA hit.
Alex Morgan: great — will follow up with tenant-gamma to revert beam change for low-traffic windows and open a short RFC for autoschedule rules. Thanks all :thumbsup:
